title: 🌐 Eryndor Living Culture Atlas XI — All Peoples by Continent & Regional Subcultures
rawNotionMarkup: Living Culture Atlas XI — regional culture crosswalk for EVERY established modeled people across ALL FIVE continents. The 28 rows reflect the 28 populations in Atlas I (all present to some degree in all five continental tallies). Each cell records possible local cultural branches, not compulsory species behavior. Drakari, Aelwyn and Living Mountains have unknown distributions and are treated separately. This is a newly authored, revisable reference that respects established geography and population allocation. It neither invents nor modifies birth rates or family sizes. ## Exiled dark mages — complete political and social isolation from outsiders (creator correction, 21 November 2026) CANON — NO OUTSIDE RELATIONS: From their formation by outcast magical practitioners at the beginning of the Era of Fire, and during their established survival well into the Third Age, the dark-mage groups of the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes did not develop relations with anyone outside their own group. They established no diplomatic relations, trade ties, alliances, treaties or cooperative political relationships with neighboring peoples, polities or communities. Treat them as an isolated power that remained apart from other societies, not a regular participant in interregional commerce, diplomacy or political coalitions. Their internal organization, personal associations among exiles, and succession across generations remain open; this does not mean they had no community among themselves. Precision: This is a correction to earlier speculative language about the mages “developing relationships with surrounding peoples.” Such external relationships did not happen. Historical encounters, threats, conflicts or observations from outsiders are not automatically established or precluded by this statement; do not invent such events. Their knowledge, exact longevity, later fate, and whether their tradition survives to the Fifth Age remain unresolved. Do not attribute dark-mage deeds to all Urakai or other inhabitants of the larger southeastern badlands region. ## Era of Fire's ending — the mages harnessed the volcano and unknowingly grew in power (creator canon, 21 November 2026) CANON EVENT AT SECOND AGE → THIRD AGE: The exiled dark mages had created the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes and its volcano through dark magic at the beginning of the Era of Fire (Second Age Year 1,322). At the end of that era (Year 1,437), planetwide earthquakes, whose aftershocks were amplified tenfold across the globe by the ancient Ironspine mountain ring, intensified their magically created volcano. The mages harnessed the power of the volcano itself to keep it from erupting with the full potential destructive force it otherwise could have had. Their intervention reduced the severity of the volcanic catastrophe; it does not establish that there was no eruption at all, no damage, or no casualties. Unforeseen effect: In channeling and restraining that volcanic power, the dark mages unknowingly acquired even greater magical power themselves. This increase in their power is an established consequence of the containment effort, although they did not know or understand it at the time. The exact metaphysical mechanism, quantitative strength increase, whether every mage gained equally, and the time and manner of any later recognition remain unknown. Their continued presence well into the Third Age is established independently; the power gain is not automatically proved to be the sole reason they survived the worldwide disaster. Continuity: The volcano was created by dark magic at the start of the Era of Fire, and was intensified by global earthquakes at the end; the mages then contained some of its destructive power, inadvertently augmenting themselves. None of this constitutes friendly diplomacy, outside alliances or trade; the dark mages remained socially and politically isolated. The origins and exact identity of their dark magical source, the exact technique for harnessing a volcanic force, and their later Third Age history remain open. Nor is a connection to the First Throne or to the separately undefined species-survival magical force established. ## Dark-mage continuity — endured well into the Third Age (creator canon, 21 November 2026) NEW CHRONOLOGICAL FACT: The dark-mage groups exiled from their villages at the beginning of the 116-year Era of Fire, who banded together in the formerly fertile southeastern agricultural lands of Avarra and deliberately created the Southern Wastes and their volcano with dark magic, were NOT confined to the Second Age. These dark-mage groups, their communities and practice continued WELL INTO THE THIRD AGE. The global earthquakes at the end of the Second Age (Second Age Year 1,437) therefore did NOT end their existence as a continuing dark-mage presence. The volcano they had created early in the Era of Fire was also intensified by the ending earthquakes; creation and later intensification are distinct events. Do not overdefine the survival: “Lasted well into the Third Age” is an intentionally broad period, not a fixed number of years or confirmation that each individual founder survived that long. The continuance may encompass successive generations, settlements, groups or traditions; the precise institutions and continuity of named founders are unwritten. Do not assign exact Third Age dates, sovereigns, wars, bloodlines, defeats, religion, expanded borders, extinction, destruction, migration, or a confirmed Fifth Age continuation. Neither their disappearance nor their survival to the present has been established. Dark magic is not attributed to an entire race, and the southern Urakai civilizations cannot be cast as the perpetrators by species. Protected chronology: (1) Second Age Year 1,322 — dark-mage exiles unite, magically transform southeastern Avarran fertile farmland into the Southern Wastes and create its volcano; (2) Second Age Year 1,437 — planetwide earthquakes shake the world, amplified tenfold globally by ancient Ironspine and intensifying the previously created volcano, ending Second Age and beginning Third Age; (3) a significant but UNNUMBERED span well into the Third Age — the dark mages endure. How they survived the natural catastrophe or interacted with the separately established yet-unidentified magical force involved in preventing species extinction is not known. First Throne involvement is an open, noncanon story option; Gloin's ancestry is unchanged and unresolved. ## Urakai / Orcs — FIRST APPEAR IN THE THIRD AGE, absent from First and Second Ages (binding creator correction, 21 November 2026) CANON CHRONOLOGICAL RULE — supersedes conflicting earlier text: Urakai (Orcs) did not exist in the First Age or anywhere in the 1,437-year Second Age. The exiled dark mages of southeastern Avarra created the Orcs sometime during the Third Age. The exact Third Age year, creation method, first location, identities of the first communities, and subsequent structure of mage–Orc command remain UNDECIDED. The Orcs were absent from the Second Age's Era of Awakening (Years 1–321), Era of Wonder (Years 322–1,321) and Era of Fire (Years 1,322–1,437). Earlier lore depicting Orc inhabitants, clans, armies, cities or events in either of those two Ages is superseded and noncanon. Goblins and Ogres may predate the Third Age. CREATOR CANON — Third Age creation and intended conquests: The exiled dark mages who formed the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes and its volcano during the Second Age survived well into the Third Age, when they created the Urakai (Orcs) by a method not yet decided. Their ambition in creating the Orcs was first to besiege the dwarven (Khazari) strongholds, and ultimately to attack the Eldar and human kingdoms. This establishes the mages' intentions, not any particular siege, conquest, campaign, chronology, victory or attack as an accomplished fact. The mages established no diplomacy, trade, treaties or alliances with pre-existing outside peoples; creating the Orcs is an act of creation for the mages' ambitions, not evidence of diplomatic relations. The exact magical or other creation process, timing, first Orc settlements, degree and duration of mage control, and later independence or resistance remain open. The modern Urakai are a diverse people with their own cultures and agency; they are not collectively evil, personally culpable for the mages' acts, or necessarily still subject to their creators. Effects on war histories: Any established older east–west wars involving Urakai, and any historical Goblin/Ogre alliances or assistance with Orc forces, must have happened in the Third Age or later, with no specific Age within that range, reign, battle, migration date or formal state assigned yet. The anti-Goblin, anti-Ogre and anti-Urakai prejudices of western Avarra remain valid consequences of those undated wars. These cannot predate the Third Age. Nor should living Urakai's settled southeast badlands homelands and their modern peoples/cultures be erased or treated as magically evil due to a speculative ancient link. Canon controls and campaign: Modern Urakai exist in large numbers, with sophisticated diverse societies, independent cities, families, economies, politics, culture and varied morality. Existing Fifth Age maps and sixfold census are unchanged; this corrects only their ancestral chronology. No changes to family rates, species lifespans or present demographics. The no-species-extinction rule at the Second Age-ending earthquake stays: Urakai were not a species that survived that disaster, because they had not appeared yet; all peoples existing at that time survived somewhere. Do not connect their origin to Gloin Hammerfeld's genuinely unknown genealogy, the First Throne, the lost First Age moon-magics or the yet-unexplained global species-survival magical force without an explicit new creator decision. ## Era of Fire — exile of dark mages and magical creation of the Southern Wastes (creator canon, 21 November 2026) CREATOR-ESTABLISHED FOUNDING EVENT, NOT A PROPOSAL: At the very beginning of the Era of Fire, the third and final era of Eryndor's 1,437-year Second Age (beginning in Second Age Year 1,322), certain groups of mages found a way to practice newly accessed dark magic. They were cast out of their home villages because of their discovery or practice. The scattered exiles banded together in the southern lands. Those lands were NOT originally wastes: they had been fertile farming country with established agricultural communities. Deliberate transformation: At the outset of the Era of Fire, the united dark mages used their new-found dark magic to transform that fertile farmland into the bleak Southern Wastes, deliberately turning productive lands into a wasteland that became their own home. The devastation is an act of the exiled mage groups, not a natural original desert, not a consequence to be misassigned to the planetwide earthquakes at the END of the Era of Fire, and not a landform that had always been infertile. These are two separate established events at opposite ends of the 116-year era. Geographical identity — CREATOR NOW FIXED: “the Southern Wastes” created by the exiled dark mages are located on AVARRA, in the SOUTHEASTERN PART OF THE CREATOR'S APPROVED CONTINENT MAP, in the portion MARKED WITH A VOLCANO. This is NOT Sahrad and must NOT be merged with Sahrad's independently established Red Wastes, Glass Desert, or Sunscorched Expanse. This confirms that the formerly fertile farming country destroyed by the exiled mages at the opening of the Era of Fire occupies part of the southeastern volcanic/badlands region of Avarra. TWO-STAGE VOLCANO HISTORY — CREATOR CORRECTION: The volcano was CREATED by the exiled mages' DARK MAGIC at the very beginning of the Era of Fire (Second Age Year 1,322), when they deliberately transformed fertile southeastern Avarran farmland into their Southern Wastes home. It did NOT exist before the dark-mage transformation and was not originally created by the earthquakes. However, at the END of the Era of Fire (Second Age Year 1,437), the planetwide earthquakes and globally tenfold-amplified aftershocks intensified the ALREADY-EXISTING MAGICAL VOLCANO. Both events shaped its present state: magical creation first, seismic intensification later. The exact volcanic response (eruption frequency, magnitude, lava fields, ash, secondary effects), whether the first magical creation involved an eruption, and particular local casualties remain unspecified. Do not erase either the original dark-magic cause or the later earthquake-driven intensification, and do not automatically attribute the entire Southern Wastes' creation to the age-ending earthquake. Exact boundaries and the specific volcano's proper name have not been supplied; don't assume every southeastern badland, every volcanic zone, or all current Urakai territory was magically transformed. Respect the many established permanent Urakai, Goblin, Ogre, Kobold, Gnome and other communities of modern southeastern Avarra; do not make Urakai responsible for the mages' act by ethnicity or geography. Their urban and pastoral communities may survive among safe valleys, wells and habitable zones in the wider southeastern region. The modern sixfold census is not changed, nor are the names or locations of any existing settlements automatically reassigned. Magic and moral distinction: Eryndor already has intrinsically good, morally grey and intrinsically evil magics. This event confirms that these mage groups gained access to and used dark magic; it does NOT yet name a source moon, deity, magical discipline, patron, spell, ritual, unique innovation or specify whether that power itself was newly born at this moment rather than newly discovered/learned by the mages. Do not equate every mage, magic user, people or regional inhabitant with these exiles. Nor is the “fire” in the Era of Fire's name yet explicitly explained by this incident alone, unless the creator decides that. Unsettled details — do not fill automatically: Exact races and numbers of mages, identities and motivations of their villages, original names and states of the farming communities, how rapidly the land transformed, what happened to the farmers, whether any groups opposed the exiles, the detailed Third Age history of their enduring settlements and magical lineage (the groups are now established as surviving well into the Third Age, but their ultimate fate remains open), and whether the dark magic connects to the First Throne or later global earthquakes are all OPEN. Do not assert an extinct species or apply modern census values to ancient populations. The creator earlier restricted free-form invention in the third era, but has now directly authorized this specific event. This historical restriction was later superseded: the creator authorized detailed Era of Fire cultures, kingdoms, rulers and wars, which are now recorded in the Era of Fire chronicle and Second Age Annals. Do not invent an unapproved additional globe-wide catastrophe, a First Throne role, or specific dark-mage encounters. Era boundary protections: The Era of Fire lasted 116 years (Years 1,322–1,437). Its ending global earthquakes reached the vastly older-than-First-Age Ironspine ring, whose central position and deep roots magnified their aftershocks tenfold across Eryndor; sudden lowland and marshland uplift (including far-western Avarran mountain creation) caused immense deaths but no species extinctions, with some protective contribution by a yet undefined magical force. The beginning dark-mage terraforming has NO established causal link to the ending earthquakes or extinction-prevention magic. The First Throne connection remains a speculative possibility, and Gloin's unknown ancestry and paused campaign are not changed. ## Era of Fire — third and final era of the Second Age, 116 years (creator canon, 21 November 2026) AVARRAN HISTORICAL NAME, CREATOR-ESTABLISHED: The third and final Avarran-defined era of Eryndor's Second Age is called the Era of Fire; other continents may name or divide the period differently. It lasted 116 years, corresponding to Second Age Years 1,322–1,437 inclusive. Its exact duration is derived from the already confirmed Second Age total: 1,437 − 321 years (Era of Awakening) − 1,000 years (Era of Wonder) = 116 years. Chronology: (1) Era of Awakening, Years 1–321, 321 years; (2) Era of Wonder, Years 322–1,321, 1,000 years; (3) Era of Fire, Years 1,322–1,437, 116 years. The catastrophic global earthquakes at the end of the Era of Fire ended the Second Age and began the Third Age. Their causes, seismic effects, sudden marshland and lowland mountain uplift, tenfold global aftershock amplification through the ancient Ironspine, mass deaths without whole-species extinction and the as-yet-undefined magical protection are recorded separately, not invented here. PARTIALLY ESTABLISHED INTERIOR — CREATOR UPDATE: The creator has now established an event at the very start of the Era of Fire: groups of mages who found access to dark magic were exiled from their villages, gathered in formerly fertile southern farming lands, and deliberately used dark magic to transform those lands into their new wasteland home (see the dedicated Era of Fire Southern Wastes section). The southeastern Avarran location of the dark-mage homeland is confirmed and regional history across all five continents has now been developed in the Second Age Annals and Era of Fire chronicle. The mages' personal identities, their exact technique, the origin of the global earthquakes, specific First Throne involvement, extra volcanic episodes and dragon cults remain open. The meaning of the word “Fire” in the era's name is not yet conclusively pinned to this event. The First Throne remains a deliberately unresolved possible thread; Gloin's unknown ancestry and campaign scene remain unaffected. ## Second Age regional cultural memory across five continents — Awakening and Wonder ONLY (creator-authorized lore, 21 November 2026) Chronological boundary: This section covers only the Era of Awakening (Second Age Years 1–321) and Era of Wonder (Years 322–1,321). It describes regional ancestral cultural development rather than asserting modern capital cities, rulers, state boundaries, present-day census allocations or current social injustices already existed. Continent names are modern map references for discussing older geography. ### Avarra — old Ironspine stone and the immense western lands Awakening: Across Ironspine's already ancient massif and the far-ranging western forests, farms and coastlands, different peoples struggled with failed or transformed lunar workings. Khazari work crews made measurable stone repair and water-storage as indispensable as runes; Eldar, Ents and forest peoples relied on living ecology and the independent World's Breath; mixed lowland settlements maintained manual grain mills, physical maps and open market weights. In eastern and southeastern lands, Goblin, Ogre, Gnome, Kobold, human and other communities faced well-and-caravan safety problems. Urakai did not exist in the Second Age and are excluded from these histories. This is not a map of Second Age states or a relocation of modern communities. Wonder: Centers of magical research, thriving forest arts, practical subterranean craft and trade among unlike peoples arose in multiple regions. Magical concealment might protect a fairy village near an otherwise ordinary market road; some mixed towns would proudly reveal themselves. Commerce connected widely separated coasts, uplands and forest belts, but not under one universal government. The Ironspine was not created during either era and no First Throne date is established here. This note does not describe the later earthquake-created mountains at Avarra's far western tip, which belong to the end of the Second Age and are outside the permitted first-two-era elaboration. ### Tharvorn — holding warmth against a changing sky Awakening: Different peoples in fjords, boreal forests and highlands developed reliable winter stores, rescue routes, ordinary sea charts and nonmagical shelters when lunar-supported protections fluctuated. Giant builders, Troll river families, human and Wolvenkin rescue groups, Merfolk shore observers and many others sometimes cooperated and sometimes quarreled over resources and passage. Wonder: New moon-born arts enriched cold-weather construction, safe navigation, highland healing and forest scholarship. Some communities shared protective enchantments through seasonal exchange; others hoarded them and charged heavy prices. Distinct northern livelihoods remained viable without assuming the modern holds or named Tharvorn settlements already existed. ### Sahrad — remembering water Awakening: River valleys, savannas, oasis regions and caravan roads suffered wherever lunar waterworks, protective rites or guidance became unpredictable. Human, Elephantfolk, Lionfolk, Centaur, Minotaur, Merfolk and other local communities developed durable reservoirs, marked wells, practical river gauges and mutual obligations around scarce water. Some rulers or guilds exploited access, while others protected it. Wonder: New magical mastery supported productive gardens, healing schools, desert wayfinding, port trade and improved large-scale water distribution in many Sahradi societies. Scholarship, livestock stewardship and practical construction did not disappear into magic. The modern Sultanates' dates, rulers and boundaries remain undecided. ### Orundel — many rivers, many experiments Awakening: Inland river communities, tropical forest peoples, highland artisans and seafarers coped with unpredictable lunar light and environmental effects using direct observation of flood seasons, soil, clouds, plant life and stone. Centaur steppe communities had different needs from Tigerfolk, Gnome, Goblin, Mushroom Folk and Human jungle or city communities, while Merfolk and Harpies maintained coastal warnings. Urakai did not yet exist; their modern Orundel communities and ancient Third-Age-or-later history are separate. Wonder: Botanical medicine, experimental moon-craft, metallurgy, irrigation, navigational signaling and elaborate artistic enchantment flourished across different societies. No single technological school, hereditary caste or government monopolized the continent's renaissance. Named present-day academies and cities are not backdated. ### Vaelora — the visible world and the concealed one Awakening: Lake inhabitants, deep-forest communities, cliff settlements and storm-coast peoples relied on ordinary navigation, refuge building, healthy soil and reciprocal aid. Fae, Pixie, Brownie, Eldar, Ent, Kobold, Troll, Ogre, Foxfolk and many others responded unevenly as lunar influences shifted; some withdrew behind wards while others built public mixed neighborhoods. Wonder: Sophisticated new lunar magic nourished both hidden fairy-tale enclaves and great public settlements. Woodland healers, lake traders, storm-watchers, cliff masons and court performers exchanged techniques where relationships permitted, while older privacy customs and ordinary craft continued. The modern Crownwall cities and Elderwood political borders are not assigned a Second Age origin. ### Cross-continental movements and cultural disagreements The millennium of Wonder was widespread prosperity and mastery, not uniformity. Knowledge travelled through family migration, trade, teaching, translation, voyages and sometimes coercion, with local peoples developing their own versions. Fae and lunar cults could be dangerous or benevolent; the same magical source might be approached under different beliefs. There were regions and households excluded from new opportunities, not an absolutely peaceful global utopia. The First Age's extinct moon-specific magics stayed extinct; learning survived through new Second Age records, not magically recovered First Age archives. Keep modern population ledger fixed and leave all Third-Era story content untouched. ## Region-first culture and species-first culture must BOTH be true An Orundel Goblin and an Avarran Goblin can share some ancestral traditions and still have different politics, diets, marriage or household customs, languages, workplaces, festivals and taboos. Meanwhile, a Goblin and a Pigfolk from the same Orundel river ward can share city identity, public holidays, navigation slang and guild membership. Do not assume the numbers of Drakari, Aelwyn or Living Mountains in any place. ## Avarra settled western expansion and southeastern Urakai badlands — creator design (21 November 2026) Creator's governing geographical settlement direction: The thousands-of-miles-wide territory between Avarra's far western coastline and the Ironspine Mountains is populated with more of the existing elder peoples, at least two distinctive human cultural regions, and Urakai societies; it is NOT a blank forest, an entirely Eldar monopoly, or an empty ocean-to-mountain stretch. The eastern and southeastern badlands/wastes must also contain substantial established Urakai (orc) populations rather than portray all orcs only in the Eastern Grasslands or all badlands as uninhabited. Both directions complement, rather than replace, the already-established Eldar Letharion High Sovereign, southern Aldermere and Valtoria, and independent Eastern Grasslands Urakai clan cities. ### Expanded west — cultural geography (new placement directions) - Deep and northern Letharion: A very large connected forest domain with multiple Eldar houses, high-canopy courts, scholar groves, river-house settlements, independent woodland communities and protected old-growth country. The High Sovereign exists, but independent councils and houses do not share a single politics. Ent grove societies and Pixie settlements occupy some woods; Aelwyn Fae may maintain seasonal court enclaves and uncommon crossings, which are not automatically public cities or universally accessible lands. Aelwyn and Pixies are separate peoples, not interchangeable 'fairies'. Drakari might have rare remote court or sanctuary territories, but no mass dragon population or exact location is declared. Smaller peoples and mixed communities (Gnomes, Halflings, Goblins, Satyrs, Brownies and others) can be substantial and culturally distinctive. - Western and southwest river valleys and foothills: Broad fertile plains and wooded belts with distinct human river-farming and inland market-town cultures, mixed with Eldar, Gnomes, Halflings and other existing peoples. Some communities can be influenced by Aldermere without automatically becoming new Aldermere provinces. Freeholders, river-canal guilds, caravan market leagues and hereditary local lords may coexist; legal/political boundaries remain open. - Far-western outer coasts and storm-facing peninsulas: Another distinct human maritime/coastal cultural grouping, with navigators, seafaring town leagues, fortified ports, weather traditions, fishing and remote island contact. These can trade with the established Shattered Coast merchant republics without silently being those same republics, Valtorian colonies or a unified new empire. Include nonhuman merchant, crafts and shore settlements, and preserve the Shattered Gulf's indented southwestern coast. - Western uplands, dry western marches and road corridors: Urakai traders, herders, mixed frontier towns and some long-standing urban or mountain-edge communities must be present west of the Ironspine too; no premise confines the species to the east. They interact through markets, treaties, cultural mixing, competing land use and at times warfare, not merely as hostile raiders. Existing northern forests and wildlands still have vast stretches of genuinely difficult terrain. ### Southeastern wastes and badlands — settled Urakai homelands (new binding habitation direction) - Urakai are long-established peoples of multiple major southeastern badlands/wastes communities since their creation sometime in the Third Age; the subsequent history of specific clans and their migrations remains open. Their presence cannot predate the Third Age. They are not just occasional invaders or temporary caravans from the eastern plains. Show recognisable permanent cities/fortified towns in canyon basins, near spring-fed rivers, protected oases and volcanic/mesa foothills, plus distributed hamlets, mine towns, road stations and migrating pastoral/clan groups. Strong enough local political institutions for law, trade, sophisticated craft, engineering, agriculture and military history. - Possible regional cultures, proposed descriptive labels not confirmed state names: canyon-basin waterwardens (reservoir builders, collective cistern laws, terrace farms), ash-ridge foundry clans (ore, ceramic craft, sophisticated metalwork and severe heat safety), salt-road caravan confederations (wells, navigation, trader treaties, mobile households), and dry-grassland edge settlements (pastoral and farm links to the Eastern Grasslands). These societies can have different dialects, governments, faiths, classes, attitudes toward outsiders and rivalries; a single 'badlands orc king' or automatic warlord state is NOT canon. - Resource/carrying capacity: Most scorched and dry interior terrain remains sparse or physically uninhabited; the substantial Urakai numbers concentrate around perennial springs, river corridors, aquifers, cistern chains, crop terraces, quarry/mineral trade, livestock routes and coastal trade access. Canals, runic/ordinary engineering, storage and imports help support larger cities but cannot erase drought, conflict or bad harvests. Populations and city sizes must be determined as nested shares of the existing numerical continent/people allocation rather than added to it. - Relations: Urakai communities of the southeastern badlands and adjoining eastern frontier can be related or competing cultures, with migration, treaty roads and trade linking the grasslands, Ironspine east/southeast foothills and far southern regions. Some populations also interact with Valtoria and local mixed peoples. No Urakai people or Urakai-specific magic is intrinsically evil on account of ancestry; actual moral character belongs to individual actions and particular magical forces. ### Demographic, religious and cartographic guardrails Under the creator's sixfold demographic model, Avarra has 1,019.760 million modeled residents, including 108 million Avarran Urakai, 72 million Avarran Eldar, and 468 million Avarran humans. The new western and southeastern communities are distributions within these already-counted figures, not extra populations added to the continental total. Aelwyn remain uncensused in the 28-people numerical matrix; do not manufacture a precise Fae census. The settlements need many thousands of miles of viable trade, farmland and transport corridors, but climate, rocky uplands, river access and wilderness create strong settlement differences. Preserve birth rates and long-lived family dynamics. In-world Gloin has not acquired an omniscient survey merely because we design one out-of-character. ## Why Goblins, Ogres and Urakai face western prejudice — older war history (21 November 2026) Creator's historical explanation: During wars between eastern and western peoples in the Third Age or later, some eastern Goblin and Ogre groups fought with or aided Urakai. Long after Goblins and Ogres moved into western lands and established ordinary, numerous communities, memory of those alliances persisted as discrimination. Western Goblins are stereotyped as thieving/conniving and widely distrusted; Ogres are widely feared, in part due to fearsome wartime reputation; rare western Urakai visitors face antipathy tied to their eastern political and military associations. These are historically inherited prejudices, not innate racial traits or proof all ancestral groups took one side. Exact dates, war names, cultures and campaigns are OPEN. The creator also raised eastern origins and the possibility that Goblins/Ogres are distinct distant biological cousins of Urakai; biological kinship is NOT established. Eastern/southeastern badlands are the main current Urakai heartlands; the Eastern Grasslands have very rare Urakai and no established Urakai settlements. Western Goblins/Ogres remain commonplace. See 03 — History & Ancient Lore for the full historical and canon-status distinction. ## Western Avarra — feared Ogres versus distrusted Goblins (creator refinement, 21 November 2026) Ogres are feared across much of western Avarra. Their size, physical power and often exaggerated reputation for violence provoke genuine apprehension: guards may be visibly tense, isolated villages nervous, innkeepers reluctant and children told frightening tales. This is a social perception, not a statement that all Ogres are violent or hostile. Ogres are common western inhabitants with their own families, villages, trades, civic lives and varied personalities. Fear may lead to exclusion or unequal treatment in some places, but no uniform kingdom-wide Ogre persecution is automatically established. Goblins are distrusted, particularly on the persistent stereotypes that they are thieving, conniving, scheming or dishonest. Those prejudices cause heavy discrimination in markets, guilds, courts, property rights and everyday dealings in many western societies. Some Goblins genuinely commit crimes, as members of any other people can; the stereotype is not an innate trait or a reliable assessment of an individual. Goblins too are common established western residents, not a universally criminal, nomadic or villainous species. Different towns, governments and individuals vary greatly in how hostile or welcoming they are. This is the latest creator clarification and supersedes any previous ambiguous claim that Ogres are simply undistinguished from other commonplace western peoples or that Goblins are the only people subjected to fear or prejudice. Neither category has fixed moral alignment, and the existing sixfold population model is unchanged. ## Earlier western social interpretation — superseded where clarified above Latest creator clarification, overriding the immediately preceding broad interpretation: Both Goblins and Ogres are common, ordinary inhabitants of western Avarra, with permanent families, villages, market districts, industries, travelling households, and all sorts of jobs and social positions. Goblins specifically experience substantial, widespread discrimination in western society. This may manifest through racist folklore, exclusionary local guilds and schools, unequal trade terms, suspicious guards, restricted civic rights or property tenure, segregated neighborhoods, hostile villages and habitual stereotyping, with actual severity varying across kingdoms, courts, regions and individual communities. Some cities recognize full equal citizenship and some Goblin institutions are powerful and independent; persistent discrimination remains an important feature of the wider western social reality. A Goblin individual's morality, honesty, intellect or occupation is not determined by those prejudices. Do not transfer Goblin-specific thieving/conniving stereotypes to Ogres: Ogres are instead widely feared for their strength and perceived dangerousness, not presumed schemers. Ogres are equally legitimate and often encountered western residents, and their size may have practical or local social consequences, but the creator's 'heavily discriminated' statement was expressly about Goblins. No uniform Ogre persecution statute is established, but fear may produce varying levels of suspicion, avoidance and discrimination. Ogres may be craftsmen, scholars, soldiers, officials, farmers, haulers, parents, wanderers, merchants or outlaws as individuals, with diverse social experiences. Neither people is a comic prop, innately evil, politically unified or required to live only in western lands. Avarra's already modeled population totals are redistributed socially and regionally without adding extra individuals or changing birth rates. ## Eastern/western Urakai placement correction — explicit creator decision (21 November 2026) Binding cartographic correction superseding earlier atlas descriptions: Urakai are a rising power in the eastern and southeastern badlands/wastes of Avarra, and may also have substantial fortified homelands in the southern mountains overlooking the Crown Sea. Other peoples and regional cultures can retain expansive kinship networks; master craft with a family, moderate craft with a family, solo master or ordinary unattached worker are options where socially appropriate. - Different priorities: Khazari widely value contribution; Eldar courts may emphasize cultivated beauty and remembered promises; Urakai clans may emphasize courage or earned trust; Aelwyn courts can prize ritual obligation; Centaur groups mobility, and so on. None is a requirement for all members. - Birth-rate freeze: No numerical adjustments or inventions to fertility, offspring, age of marriage, birth intervals, population totals or lifespans. New subculture descriptions are not demographic mechanics. - Real work: Cooking, caregiving, farming, artistry, priesthood, soldiering, scholarship, trade, hygiene work, child-raising and repair all contribute to lived civilization. A people may see esteem differently from another. - Local tensions: Social judgment depends on court and class. A wealthy port court may prize fashion while its dock families value loyalty; both are local. Refugees, forced migrants and war captives can preserve their old customs or develop new mixed communities. ## Rare or uncounted peoples — no invented geography - Drakari: Sovereign courts, solitary territories and unaligned scholars can hold differing customs, but no fixed continent distribution or population tally is established. - Aelwyn: Season-based court customs, unaligned wanderers and local pact traditions may not obey ordinary geographical borders. Do not force a reliable census into the Atlas I table. - Living Mountains: Their number, locations, origins, family and culture remain unknown. This atlas cannot truthfully list named tribes or group traditions for them yet; the unknown is intentional. - All other established intelligent peoples are included in the 28-row crosswalk above, plus fully differentiated subcultures in Atlas VIII, IX and X. ## Persistent culture simulation in actual play When Gloin reaches a village, hamlet, city or caravan camp, the GM should track the culture on three overlapping levels: 1. Regional civic culture: state law, local economy, water/food, holidays, public spaces, social classes and military/security obligations. 2. Communities and subcultures: neighborhood, species, profession, adopted family, migrant networks and political groups; each community may have multiple opinions. 3. Actual individuals: people with their own ambitions, contradictions, risks, work, relationships and history. Nobody is just a stereotype from a species entry. Generate a small number of specific, memorable customs for a particular place—perhaps a fair, ceremonial exchange, holiday dish, marriage practice, market bargaining taboo, river funeral custom, old feud, worker's union, game, seasonal caravan rite or court greeting—and maintain them consistently after they are introduced. Give customs social reasons, not just random novelty. Regional time and law govern whether outsiders understand or are allowed to participate. A mixed village's local practice might be shared across several species. A coastal branch of one people might reject the social norms of its homeland. A new profession or faith might eventually produce another subculture.
